issues.location: LP and Halldén matrix languages, source lines 22 and 33
issues.finding: Both matrices call their language standard L_0 but list truth functions only for negation, conjunction, disjunction and conditional; Halldén additionally interprets plus. The earlier L_0 formation rules may include nullary constants and other connectives under reader tags, but these are not interpreted here. The LP tautology proof's induction base covers variables alone.
issues.proposed_resolution: Define LP and Halldén on the constant-free fragment generated by propositional variables and the four listed connectives, with Halldén's plus as its extra connective. Keep the LP theorem in that defined scope.

issues.finding: The base asserts v(p)=v'(p) without qualification, although the preceding definition maps v(p)=Undef to v'(p)=True. The two induction implications are still true: their antecedents concern only v(p)=False or True, while both antecedents fail at Undef.
issues.proposed_resolution: Scope the displayed equality to the False and True cases and state that the Undef case makes both induction antecedents false.

issues.finding: Two expressions put the logic index between the valuation and formula arguments of the value macro, unlike the source's own standard form and the intended equalities.
issues.proposed_resolution: Write pValue_v(A)[Ks] and pValue_v'(A)[CL] with the formula argument before the optional logic index in both target expressions.

issues.location: LP proof conjunction induction step, source lines 108 and 114
issues.finding: The false and true conjunction cases each repeat the value of B where the second premise must concern C. The following induction-hypothesis sentences already use B and C respectively.
issues.proposed_resolution: Replace the second B by C in both displayed premise pairs, preserving the rest of the conjunction argument.

issues.location: shared classical tautologies after Halldén's plus extension
issues.finding: The unqualified claim that both logics have the same tautologies as classical logic compares different languages: Halldén's language has the additional plus operator, which ordinary classical propositional logic lacks. The preceding exercise establishes preservation of classical tautologies, and equality is meaningful on the shared four-connective fragment.
issues.proposed_resolution: Qualify the equality claim as applying to the common fragment without the extra operator; retain the claim that the consequence relations differ.

translation_treatment: The target translates both designated-value logics, the LP theorem and induction, consequence exercises, R-Mingle, and the Gödel designation result. It narrows matrix language scope, fixes the conditional induction base, places two logic indices consistently, corrects both repeated conjunction operands, and qualifies the cross-language tautology comparison. Frozen source is unchanged.
